target: ACT-PLT-10 Maintenance engineering (platform)
claim_challenged: 800 h/yr fixed maintenance (48,000 min base), the largest fixed engineering load, active from 0 customers
challenge: The engineering rows apply no native/AI reduction at all: conventional_minutes equals base minutes for ACT-PLT-10 (48,000=48,000), PLT-04, PLT-07, PLT-12, PLT-13, while every operations row is cut 2-10x versus conventional. The package itself buys EXP-AI-02 AI tooling 'for maintenance' but credits no hours for it. A modular monolith on managed PostgreSQL/Fargate with Renovate/Dependabot auto-PRs, CI and signed builds has a bounded annual change load: tax-year/Nacha rule updates (~60-80 h), dependency and runtime upgrades largely auto-generated (~100 h review/fix), deprecations (~40 h), defect fixing (~150-200 h). 800 h is a conventional half-FTE allowance carried over from Phase II (SRC-ZB-002/003 are not workload measurements).
evidence: activities.csv ACT-PLT-10 minutes 30000/48000/72000 and conventional_minutes 48000 (identical); EXP-AI-02 purpose 'Coding and analysis assistants for maintenance'; architecture-obligations.md s1 (single managed cluster, no broker in release 1); tornado: ACT-PLT-10 swing $81.1k on L first-customer cash. Rerun of the shipped model in scratchpad with PLT-10 400 h plus the PLT-04/09/13/07 changes below: L first-customer cash $306.0k -> $213.4k; L first employee 4 -> 9 customers; zero-customer cash $44.6k -> $7.1k.
proposed_change: ACT-PLT-10 minutes 15000/24000/42000 (250/400/700 h); keep high at 700 h for an immature codebase; add a note that the first 12 months after launch may run at the high end, then decay.

target: Engine.applyCoverage (COV-CHG, COV-BRK, COV-ONC, COV-OPS)
claim_challenged: Coverage persons counted = employees + founder only; contracted hours never count as a distinct qualified person
challenge: At L/1 customer the model already buys ~620 contract engineering hours (a named contractor working ~40% time) and then additionally buys $52k of reviewers, $12k break-glass holder and $36k secondary on-call as if no second engineer existed. A contractor with ~600 h/yr of production work is exactly the person who can be secondary on-call, second break-glass activator and one non-author approver; the requirement (CNV-PLT-010) asks for distinct approvers, not employees, and ORG-R14 states the on-call role can_be_fractional=Y and can_be_outsourced=Y. Same pattern in T/F: ~300 contracted operations hours plus a $40k COV-OPS backup retainer.
evidence: Engine.fs applyCoverage: have = employees0 + (founder?1:0); roles.jsonl:14 ORG-R14 can_be_fractional Y, can_be_outsourced Y; headline.csv L,1: labor_cash $234.5k of which coverage alternatives $100k and contract hours 1,124; workload.csv engineering fixed ~1,529 h at 1 customer.
proposed_change: Count a contracted engineer (or operations analyst) with >=400 h/yr in the role as one person for COV-CHG, COV-BRK, COV-ONC and COV-OPS, plus an explicit standby/availability premium (base $6k/yr, range $3k-12k) for on-call. At L/1 this removes the COV-BRK and COV-ONC alternatives and one of two COV-CHG reviewers: about -$65k to -$75k first-customer cash (T/F: about -$95k to -$105k incl. COV-OPS).

target: COV-CHG alternative (contracted independent reviewer)
claim_challenged: $26k/yr per reviewer (~200 h at $130) and two reviewers = $52k/yr at the first customer
challenge: Workload arithmetic from the model's own inputs: ACT-PLT-03 assumes 100 changes/yr; CNV-PLT-010 binds only changes to control-relevant modules (gate, ledger, reservations, holds, authority, dispatch), plausibly <=50% of changes. 50 changes x 2 reviewers x 45 min = 75 reviewer-hours/yr = ~$9.8k at $130 for both reviewers, not $52k. AI cannot be an approver (UNB-AI-STD-003: agents may not self-approve) but AI pre-review legitimately shortens human review minutes. A retainer with a small monthly minimum plus per-review hourly billing fits; a partner's engineers (W) could serve as an in-kind independent approver under contract.
evidence: unbound/requirements/PLATFORM-UX-API-AND-ASSURANCE-STANDARDS.md:312 CNV-PLT-010 ('Modules tagged control-relevant ... SHALL require two approvers on every change, neither the author'); :45 UNB-AI-STD-003; activities.csv ACT-PLT-03 rate 50/100/200 x 40 min; coverage.csv COV-CHG alt 13000/26000/50000; tornado COV-CHG swing $74k.
proposed_change: COV-CHG alt_annual per reviewer 4000/8000/20000 (30-150 h at contract rate, monthly minimum included); add a control-module change share parameter (0.3/0.5/0.8) so reviewer cost scales with ACT-PLT-03. Combined with ADV-O-02, COV-CHG at first customer ~ $8k instead of $52k.

target: COV-ONC two-deep on-call (contract-typical, from customer 1)
claim_challenged: A $36k/yr contracted secondary on-call is needed from the first customer
challenge: No numeric SLA exists or may be offered until benchmark and pilot evidence (XID-SAS-004: 'numeric commitments only after evidence'; obligations s8 'No contractual SLAs until benchmark and pilot'). The model's own incident load is 12 incidents x 4 h = 48 h/yr (ACT-PLT-01). $36k for 48 incident-hours is ~$750 per incident-hour. Two-deep comes from an adversarial review cited in ORG-R14, not a contract. For a pilot-stage sponsor with capability SLOs, founder primary plus pay-per-incident contractor (LAB-31 contract SRE $49-150/h) with a modest standby fee is adequate, and degraded-mode design (UNB-AVL-011: refuse new work, status page; holds never queued) limits harm from a slower response.
evidence: unbound/requirements/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md XID-SAS-004; architecture-obligations.md s2 and s8; roles.jsonl:14 (minimum_count sourced to review-arch-econ.md); prices-ops.csv LAB-31 ('No public on-call premium/retainer benchmark found'); activities.csv ACT-PLT-01 12 x 240 min.
proposed_change: COV-ONC alt_annual 3000/9000/18000 (standby fee + per-incident hours); trigger only when a contract with a numeric response objective is signed (make trigger a contract flag or customers>=2), keep tier-2 COV-ONC24 unchanged. With ADV-O-02 it is met by the contracted engineer at no extra alternative.

target: roles.csv hire_threshold_hours (engineering 800; operations 800; compliance 800; implementation 800; support 900)
claim_challenged: Residual work above 800 h is employed rather than contracted
challenge: The threshold is not cost-minimising. At the model's own prices an engineering employee costs $196.5k vs residual contract hours at $130: break-even = 196,503/130 = 1,511 h. Hiring at 801 h costs $196.5k against $104k contracted (+$92k). Equivalent break-evens: implementation 140,000/110 = 1,273 h; operations 120,925/85 = 1,423 h; compliance 116,662/110 = 1,060 h; support 65,167/50 = 1,303 h. The rule converts a contracting decision into a conventional headcount decision.
evidence: roles.csv loaded_annual_base and contract_hourly_base; Engine.staffRole byLoad rule. Scratchpad rerun with break-even thresholds: L first employee 4 -> 5 customers, W 5 -> 6, T 2 -> 3; L cash at 10 customers $521k -> $480k.
proposed_change: Set hire_threshold_hours = loaded_annual / contract_hourly per role (engineering 1511, implementation 1273, operations 1423, compliance 1060, support 1303), or let the engine choose the cheaper of hire vs contract like it does for coverage; allow a non-cost override only with a cited reason (e.g. continuity).

target: ACT-IMP-01 Customer onboarding (300 h per new customer)
claim_challenged: Flat 18,000 min per new customer for every profile, with no learning curve

Data migration is excluded (model M carries it). The same 300 h is charged for a 60-account XS foundation as for a 6,000-account L sponsor, and for customer #10 as for #1. target: COV-OPS business-day continuity (T, F)
claim_challenged: $40k/yr contracted backup operations analyst at the first customer

Business-day continuity (exceptions within sponsor-set business days, complaint acknowledgment in 2 business days, CNV-PLT-005) at ~300 h/yr workload (~1.2 h/business day) is met by a second analyst on call-off at hourly rates.

target: Engine.newCustomers / parameter new_customer_share
claim_challenged: At 1-4 customers the model onboards and sells one new customer every year (max 1, round(n x 0.3))
challenge: The 'annual cost at n customers' embeds a full acquisition and onboarding every year even when n is static: at n=1 that is 300 h implementation ($33k) + 160 founder h displaced to contract ($20.8k) + $5k counsel = ~$59k. This is growth investment, not operating cost; it inflates run-rate, break-even customer counts and the 'can the first customer finance the next' table (s11), which then double-counts the next customer's acquisition.
evidence: Engine.fs newCustomers: 'max 1.0 (Math.Round(float n * new_customer_share))'; parameters.csv new_customer_share basis 'at least one in any year with customers'; workload.csv ACT-IMP-01 300 h at 1 customer.
proposed_change: Report run-rate (new customers = 0) and growth cost separately; compute break-even on run-rate and treat acquisition+onboarding as a per-customer investment recovered over contract life. Run-rate at L/1 drops ~ $50-60k.

A partner-first channel does NOT remove the need (a partner's SOC would carve out or include EF), so keep Type II from year 2.

proposed_change: EXP-SEC-04 amount 7000/9000/20000 and activate from the second customer-year (or a first_year=0 flag); first-customer cash -$12k, steady state -$3k.

target: COV-BRK two-person break-glass
